T1 LOCK A

T2 LOCK B
T2 WAIT A

proposal.diagnosis: The program deadlocks because the two threads acquire the mutexes in opposite order (T1 locks A then B, T2 locks B then A) and then wait at a barrier while each holds one mutex, creating a circular wait condition.
proposal.root_cause: Inconsistent lock acquisition order: each thread locks its own 'first' mutex based on its ID before the barrier, then attempts to lock the other 'second' mutex after the barrier, leading to a lock order reversal between threads.
proposal.reasoning_summary: All three runs show the same cyclic lock wait pattern (A→B, B→A). Enforcing a global lock order (always A then B) eliminates the circular wait while preserving the barrier synchronization and logging.
proposal.expected_effect: The program will no longer deadlock; both threads will acquire mutex A then B, pass the barrier, release locks, and print PASS.
risk_notes: Alters which mutex each thread locks first (output order of lock messages changes).
Assumes locking A then B is acceptable for the program's correctness; if the algorithm relied on the original lock ordering, behavior may differ.
Potential minor performance impact due to always locking A first, but negligible.
